content:
marta: Quick q about GCP KMS for Private deploys — what's our recommended pattern for service accounts and key rings? Customer-owned keyring vs Redwood-managed? Minimal IAM for runtime; rotation approach w/out downtime?

sam: My recommendation: customer holds keyring/cryptoKey in their project. Runtime SA (deployer runtime) in customer project with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the cryptoKey only. Redwood components that need to rewrap or manage keys should use impersonation rather than broad project roles.

alex: Envelope pattern we use: generate per-customer DEK (data encryption key) inside Redwood, encrypt DEK with customer's KMS key => store ciphertext. At runtime we decrypt the DEK (via KMS) and use DEK locally for low-latency ops. Rotation: create new CryptoKeyVersion, update metadata so new DEKs are wrapped with new version, and run a background rewrap job to re-encrypt stored DEKs. Support reading with multiple key versions during migration to avoid downtime.

nish: Important: enable Cloud KMS Data Access logs for the customer project (they're off by default). Encrypt/Decrypt show up as
- google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Encrypt
- google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt
Export to BigQuery or GCS for retention + alert on unexpected high decrypts.

sam: Also keep IAM tight — grant the runtime SA the role on the specific cryptoKey resource, not project-wide. Example commands:
```
# create keyring + key
gcloud kms keyrings create redwood-customer --location=global --project=customer-project
gcloud kms keys create app-encrypt-key --location=global --keyring=redwood-customer --purpose=encryption --project=customer-project

# grant runtime SA encrypt/decrypt
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding app-encrypt-key \
  --location=global --keyring=redwood-customer \
  --member='serviceAccount:sa-runtime@customer-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com' \
  --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' --project=customer-project
```
If Redwood needs to run rewrap jobs, we either (A) run a job inside customer's project (preferred), or (B) grant a minimal impersonation binding so a Redwood service account can impersonate a short-lived rewrap SA in the customer project.

sec-ops-bot: Noted. Please add the choose-your-risk matrix to the runbook: customer-owned keyring vs redwood-owned, and include sample IAM snippets + audit log checklist. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-private

marta: Thanks, this helps. I'll draft a PR for the runbook with the commands + rotation playbook. Will @sam and @nish review?

sam: yep, happy to.
